title: One emission step
statement: Let $c$ be a program, let $x$ be a bridge-alphabet input, let $p$ be a valid input-head position, and let $st$ assign stack words to the four stack names. Suppose the main stack begins with the bit symbol for a Boolean $b$, followed by a stack word $xs$. In one step from the emitting state with optional pending bit $carry$, the bridging machine removes that first symbol, enters the emitting state with pending bit $b$, leaves the input-head position and other stacks unchanged, and appends $carry$ to the output if it is present.
hypotheses_covered: The main stack equals the bit symbol for $b$ followed by $xs$
replaced:
Suppose the bridging machine is in the emitting state with an optional pending bit,
and the main stack begins with the bit symbol embedding a Boolean $b$.  Then a
single step pops that symbol, appends the pending bit (if present, embedded into the
bridge alphabet) to the output, and continues in the emitting state with pending bit
$b$; the input position and the other stacks are unchanged.
